title: On the Moments of Least $s$-Gaps of Partitions and a Conjecture of Baruah and Talukdar
summary: Andrews and Newman \cite{AN19, AN20} defined the minimal excludant or mex of a partition. The mex of a partition is the smallest positive integer which is absent from the partition. Baruah, Bhoria, Eyyunni and Maji \cite{BBEM} studied the sum of mex split according to parity, together with its $\ell$-th moments. Ballantine and Merca \cite{BM20} generalized mex to the least $s$-gap, which is the smallest natural number that does not occur minimum $s$ times in the partition.
